signals.title: USD/CAD — Geopolitical Supply Shock & Labor Divergence
signals.text: CAD COT LF short -82,720 contracts (21.2% long) sets up positioning vulnerability as Strait of Hormuz tanker explosions push crude supply risks higher into the weekly open. Weekend reports of naval mine strikes in Hormuz lift WTI oil above $91.80/bbl, countering the drag from Canada's severe 68.3k employment contraction. The Sydney open and subsequent European energy desk pricing resolve whether crude gains overwhelm domestic macro weakness. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD into the open as crude price spikes challenge Friday's 1.4254 close. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo market open and energy market response to Hormuz escalation. Risk: Break above 1.4300 if crude fades and markets focus exclusively on the BoC pause narrative.

signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Energy Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard establishes NOK as the primary outperformer (+0.986%, n=2) against EUR as the laggard (-0.669%, n=9) for a 1.655% spread, reinforced by weekend Hormuz disruptions driving crude supply premia. European energy terms of trade deteriorate under Middle East shipping threats while Norway captures positive terms-of-trade inflows, compounding Norges Bank's restrictive +1.82% real rate against the ECB's +0.30%. The Tokyo session and Monday 06:00 UTC German CPI release determine EUR sensitivity to inflation-adjusted real yield compression. Trade bias: Long NOK/EUR into Sunday open. Catalyst: Sydney open energy pricing followed by German CPI release on 12 Oct at 06:00 UTC. Risk: De-escalation of Gulf shipping threats or German CPI topping 3.3% YoY to spark ECB rate support.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Speculative Long Unwind Risk
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +48,911 contracts (70.3% long) leaves the pair vulnerable to positioning liquidations after failing to reclaim the 20-day SMA at 0.7033 on Friday's 0.6988 close. While AONIA-SOFR yields grant a +73bp OIS carry advantage to AUD, heightened cross-asset bond volatility (MOVE index at the 94th percentile) and broader USD yield support restrain topside continuation. Governor Waller's speech on 12 Oct at 07:45 UTC tests whether the Fed pause thesis holds against elevated US 2Y yields at 4.75%. Trade bias: Short AUD/USD on intraday rallies toward 0.7010. Catalyst: Fed Governor Waller speech on 12 Oct at 07:45 UTC. Risk: Sustained break above the 200-day SMA at 0.7040 invalidates the short bias.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Extreme Options Put Skew
signals.text: JPY COT LF net short -30,379 contracts alongside a 264bp SOFR-TONA carry buffer maintains fundamental upside support toward 158.25 despite persistent jawboning risk. Options 25-delta risk reversals exhibit an aggressive put skew of -1.88, reflecting heavy institutional demand for downside tail hedges should safe-haven flows accelerate. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 30 Oct and Tokyo liquidity depth at the session open serve as catalysts for testing whether spot breaches the 200-day SMA at 158.52. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY above 158.00 on carry dominance. Catalyst: Tokyo session cash open and next BoJ meeting on 30 Oct. Risk: Daily close below the 20-day SMA at 157.27 triggered by safe-haven flight.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short Base vs Inflation Catalyst
signals.text: EUR COT LF short -84,775 contracts (4th percentile of 52-week range) positions the euro for potential short-covering squeezes following Friday's 1.1206 close. Extreme leveraged short positioning clashes with an undervalued BEER model misvaluation of z = -2.27σ, even as Fed-ECB OIS carry favors the dollar by +143bp. ECB holds at 2.65%. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD with upside squeeze risks toward 1.1280. Catalyst: Germany CPI release on 12 Oct at 06:00 UTC (forecast 3.3% YoY). Risk: Print below 3.1% YoY accelerates selling toward the 1.1150 handle.
